players.product: obesity and metabolic-disease therapeutics; multispecific protein therapeutics designed with The Generate Platform

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Zealand Pharma's Metabolic Frontier 2030 ambition, kicked off in December last year, targets five products on the market in 2030, a pipeline of 10 clinical programs and industry-leading times from idea to clinic; by 2030 he hopes Zealand will be launching its first product alongside Roche Genentech into a very consumer-driven market, and Zealand is investing in building a fully integrated presence, including commercial presence, to support such a launch.
quarterly_data.figure: five products on the market in 2030; 10 clinical programs

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: in the coming four or five years Zealand is going to spend five times as much on research alone as it did in the past five years, around $800 million into research alone; in a few weeks it will open a Cambridge, Massachusetts research site equally sized to its Denmark research group (20 to 30 of the people who will work there already signed in), going beyond peptides into other modalities; it expects more partnerships with modality-based platform companies in the metabolic space, as it did with OTR Therapeutics last year on small molecules. After petrelintide, investing in the pipeline is its key second priority.
quarterly_data.figure: around $800 million into research alone; five times as much on research as in the past five years

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: the phase II program for petrelintide tested five different doses with a lot of patients in each arm and delivered double-digit weight loss with a placebo-like tolerability profile; Zealand is moving into phase III together with Roche with confidence in the dose setting, with the program focused on speed to market to be among the first to launch into the amylin category. A smaller phase II study of petrelintide in obese individuals living with type 2 diabetes will read out later this year.
quarterly_data.figure: five different doses tested in phase II; double-digit weight loss

quarterly_data.signal: CEO on the obesity market: if you ask patients, four out of five would give a weight-loss target below 20%; with GLP-1s many patients stop within a month and after a year probably only 20% to 30% are still on treatment; he thinks around 60%-70% of all scripts are a patient-initiated conversation; 3% to 5% of patients are being treated today in the U.S.; he expects the next battle to be the best tolerability at the weight loss patients want, rather than a few percent more weight loss.
quarterly_data.figure: four out of five patients want weight loss below 20%; around 60%-70% of scripts patient-initiated (CEO view)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: the Roche partnership gives Zealand shared economics on both petrelintide and the combination product; the ZINERGI phase II study now starting is a dose-finding study balancing the GLP-1/GIP component CT-388 with the amylin component petrelintide, positioned for patients who already benefit from one of the two components (he notes 15% of patients do not respond to a GLP-1).
quarterly_data.figure: shared economics on petrelintide and the combination

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: survodutide is licensed to Boehringer, which is fully responsible for clinical development and commercialization; Zealand receives high single to low double-digit royalties. Boehringer's phase III data at ADA showed around 16% to 17% weight loss, predominantly liver and visceral fat, with only 10% muscle loss versus the 20% to 30% seen with other GLP-1s; the rest of the obesity phase III program reports this year, the cardiovascular outcome study (CVOT) should read out later this year, a large MASH program including end-stage liver disease reads out in the coming years, and (he thinks in August) Boehringer started a phase III study in type 2 diabetes.
quarterly_data.figure: high single to low double-digit royalties; 16% to 17% weight loss in phase III

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Zealand will resubmit dasiglucagon for congenital hyperinsulinism to the FDA in the second half and hopes to have it approved next year; in parallel it is in partnership discussions, aiming to partner its rare disease assets with a dedicated rare disease company, starting with the U.S.
quarterly_data.figure: FDA resubmission in the second half; approval hoped for next year

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: for glepaglutide in short bowel syndrome, Zealand started the second phase III study earlier this year to support U.S. approval based on FDA feedback (up and running and recruiting); the EU file was submitted last year and it should hear back from the EU this year; it wants a partner and could start partnership discussions later this year. He describes the market, with the short-acting product available today, as north of DKK 1 billion in sales.
quarterly_data.figure: second phase III recruiting; EU decision expected this year; market north of DKK 1 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: earlier this year Zealand initiated a phase Ib/IIa study of its Kv1.3 blocker in patients living with psoriasis and has already seen receptor engagement and effects on the targeted immune pathways in early exposure; it will soon start another smaller study in another indication and envisions partnering the program with a more established player in the autoimmune space.

CEO: news flow over the next 12 to 18 months includes the petrelintide phase III kick-off and recruitment progress, the phase II petrelintide readout in type 2 diabetes later this year, the combination studies kicking off, further survodutide phase III data including the CVOT later this year and later the MASH program, the Kv1.3 program, the EMA decision on glepaglutide, the dasiglucagon (CHI) FDA resubmission and potential partnerships.
